title: Monaco Win in Paris to Reclaim the French Title and Complete a Quadruple
description: Monaco are champions of France once again, winning a wild and dramatic Game 5 at the Adidas Arena 101-92 against Paris Basketball to take the Betclic Elite title a third crown in four years and the final piece of an unprecedented quadruple this season, achieved just before the team is broken up this summer. The decider delivered on every promise, and the drama began hours before tip-off with the announcement that Matthew Strazel (184-PG-2002) had been suspended for the game. Monaco's response was a stunner: they activated Mike James (185-PG-1990, college: Lamar), the American playmaker who had been absent since May 5 and on strike over unpaid wages at the club. Wearing the number 32 Strazel's number James did not weigh heavily on the game for long, but he was among the Monaco players who turned it around at the start of the fourth quarter. With the Roca Team seemingly buckling, trailing…
imageCaption: Monaco Win in Paris to Reclaim the French Title and Complete a Quadruple (Photo: Monaco)

title: Paris Basketball claim Betclic ELITE ProA title
description: Paris - Monaco 99-93 Paris Basketball claimed Elite ProA title. They went on a furious run in the fourth quarter to snatch the victory against Monaco in the decisive fifth game of the championship series. Monaco was trailing by 4 points at halftime but managed to get 8-point lead after three quarters before a 26-12 charge of Paris Basket, which allowed them to win the game. 26 personal fouls committed by Monaco helped opponents get some easy free throw opportunities. American-North Macedonian point guard TJ Shorts (175-1997, college: UC Davis) orchestrated the victory with a double-double by scoring 27 points, 7 rebounds and 10 assists. The former international guard Nadir Hifi (188-2002) contributed with 16 points for the winners. Shorts is a former Eurobasket Summer League player, which is considered top international summer league in the market. Paris Basket's coach used an…
imageCaption: Paris Basketball claim Betclic ELITE ProA title (Photo: Betclic ELITE)

title: Paris claim Leaders Cup title
description: Paris - Nanterre 90-85 Paris earned their first ever Leaders Cup title. They overpowered Nanterre for the trophy tonight. TJ Shorts (175-PG-1997, college: UC Davis) stepped up with 26 points for the winning side. Paris sank 26 points in the opening quarter to gain a 6-point lead. They maintained the lead throughout the second period. Paris established a 48-42 halftime lead. Nanterre responded with a furious third-quarter rally. They erased the deficit and snatched a 69-65 lead at the final break. But Paris quickly regained composure. They bounced back with a 25-16 surge in the final term to claim a historic win. Nadir Hifi (188-G-2002) recorded 20 points in the victory. Justin Bibbins (176-PG-1996, college: Utah) responded with 20 points, while Desi Rodriguez (197-F-1996, college: Seton Hall) notched 15 points in the defeat.
imageCaption: Monaco cruise past Paris to claim LNB title (Photo: lnb.azureedge.net)

title: Monaco clinch first ever Betclic ELITE ProA title
description: Levallois - Monaco 85-92 Monaco celebrated the first ever Pro A title. They stole a road win over Levallois to complete the sweep of the championship series. The guests trailed by 9 points after first quarter, but they rallied back getting tie in the second period and winning the second half and won the game by 7 points. Monaco made 18-of-21 free shots (85.7 percent) during the game. The best player for the winners was American swingman Jordan Loyd (193-1993, college: Indianapolis) who scored 22 points. His fellow American import forward Jaron Blossomgame (199-1993, college: Clemson) chipped in 22 points. Monaco's coach Sasa Obradovic used a ten-player rotation which allowed the starters a little rest for the next games. title: ASVEL celebrate Jeep ELITE ProA title
description: Dijon - ASVEL 74-87 ASVEL have been crowned Jeep Elite Pro A champions. They overcame Dijon in the Final in Rouen tonight. The game was mostly controlled by ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne Basket. JDA Dijon managed to win fourth quarter 23-20. But it was not enough to take a lead and get a victory that evening. ASVEL Lyon-Villeurbanne Basket made 17-of-20 free shots (85.0 percent) during the game. They looked well-organized offensively handing out 22 assists. Worth to mention a great performance of swingman David Lighty (198-88, college: Ohio St.) who helped to win the game recording 21 points and 5 assists. He was named the MVP. The former international point guard Antoine Diot (192-89) contributed with 14 points, 6 rebounds and 6 assists for the winners.
